messages:
sam: FYI customer reported streaming responses that break JSON parsing mid-object. happens intermittently on gosdk 0.13.2 when proxying through their internal gateway.
rachel: ugh. any logs or small repro? :eyes:
sam: pasted minimal repro below. request stream -> server sends chunked responses; one chunk ends inside an object. gosdk scanner throws: \"unexpected EOF while scanning object\". log snippet:
```
recv: '{"id":1,"text":"hello'
recv: ' world","meta":{'
recv: '"k":"v"}}\n'
error: scanner: unexpected EOF
```
vince: that looks like chunk boundary fragmentation. do we see any truncation on server side or only in client? have they tested curl stream directly?
sam: they did. curl --no-buffer against hosted API returns same split chunks but curl will show concatenated stream so downstream parser didn't fail. seems gosdk scanner is stricter.
kevin: which reader path in gosdk? the streaming scanner tries to decode incremental json objects using bufio.Scanner with a token size limit. if a chunk splits a very long token, Scanner can fail with bufio.ErrTooLong. but error here is unexpected EOF — parser noticed incomplete object and returned.
eng-sre-bot: deploy-bot: new rollouts none.
rachel: steps I asked customer to try: 1) upgrade to gosdk 0.14.0 (we fixed several scanner/fragmentation regressions) 2) set ReadBufferSize override in client config 3) try toggling http/1.1 vs http/2 on their proxy.
sam: they tried 0.14.0 and still saw edge cases but much less frequent. interestingly, adding a tiny client-side reassembly buffer (read until matching braces) eliminated failures.
vince: ok, two hypotheses: (A) proxy is injecting chunk boundaries arbitrarily (ok) and our scanner/decoder doesn't robustly handle split tokens (fixable); (B) server may be returning intermediate partial JSON flushes (intentional for latency) and clients must treat stream as framing-delimited objects.
kevin: proposed short-term mitigation: catch scanner errors and attempt small backoff + re-read last N bytes to complete object. long-term: move gosdk to a framing protocol where server emits \n-delimited JSON (ndjson) or explicit content-length per object in streaming responses.
sam: customer also reported auth 401 after retry floods when client retries on partial parse errors. their gateway treats the follow-up as new requests and trips rate-limits.
rachel: can you add retry guard to docs: do not re-issue failed requests blindly on parse errors for streaming — prefer to resume or re-fetch from last known cursor.
vince: logging notes for eng-runtime: add chunk boundary metric and a counter for \"partial-object parse failures\" so we can correlate with proxy patterns.
kevin: quick repro command we used (for eng):
```
go run ./cmd/stream-repro --endpoint https://api.redwood.dev/stream --sdk-version 0.13.2 --proxy http://local-proxy:3128
```
this outputs raw chunk boundaries and parser errors.
eng-sre-bot: created ticket INF-4321 linking logs and proxy headers.
sam: customer accepted workaround (upgrade+buffer) for now. want eng to triage on Monday: (1) confirm bufio.Scanner token sizing and fallback, (2) propose ndjson framing opt-in, (3) docs/faq about retry behavior for streams.
rachel: noted. i'll add to support KB and reassign to eng-runtime. thx all :heart:
